result:
The proposed answer of 8 is very likely wrong. I did not re-derive the true maximum, so the correct value below rests on my recollection of this known problem, which I believe is 3.

Two problems stand out in the solution:

- **Shared start vertex.** All assistants start together at one vertex and must leave it along the three edges there. The edge-disjoint partition assumes assistants can immediately occupy separate edge sets, such as a 6-cycle away from the start vertex. The claim that transient collisions in the first step are harmless "because r=0" is asserted rather than checked. For example, three fast assistants cannot all reach a 6-cycle disjoint from the start edges without sharing edges along the way.
- **Unproved optimality.** The claim that 8 is the maximum rests only on an edge-counting argument ("all 12 edges used"). That argument is not valid, because assistants can share edges when their timing makes every meeting fall at a vertex.

VERDICT: REJECT
